title: Shelving unfinished work
summary: git stash: switch branches without committing half-done work.

say.never: Imagine you're halfway through something that isn't ready to save, and a teammate asks you to fix a small bug on another branch *right now*. Git won't let you switch branches if it would overwrite your unfinished work. A **stash** is a shelf: put your unfinished work on it, switch and fix the bug, come back, and take your work off the shelf.
say.bit: Stash shelves uncommitted changes so you can switch branches (git refuses to switch when your changes would be overwritten), then `stash pop` restores them.

say.never: Click the **Source Control** icon on the left: the one that looks like a branch.

Look at the very bottom of the window. The name just left of the branch is the repository you're working on. Click it and choose **08-stash** from the list at the top. Source Control now shows only that repository.
say.bit: Bottom-left, click the repository name and choose **08-stash**.

say.never: Click the branch name in the bottom-left and pick `develop`. A message says your local changes would be overwritten. That's exactly the problem a stash solves. Press **Cancel**. Don't press **Force Checkout**: it throws your work away.
say.bit: Click the branch name, pick `develop`, and see the warning. Press **Cancel**, not **Force Checkout**.

say.never: Point at the **CHANGES** heading in Source Control. A **...** button (More Actions) appears at its right end. Click it. It works on the repository you picked.
Point at **Stash** in the menu, then click **Stash** at the top of the second menu. When it asks for a stash message, just press **Enter**. Your changes go on the shelf.

Click the branch name in the bottom-left and switch to `develop`. Change "Teh" to "The" in `Notes.md` and save. Find `Notes.md` in Source Control, stage it with **+**, then type a message and press **Commit**.
